title: Config circuit-breaker with policy simulation and progressive rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope
Implement a 'circuit-breaker' style automated config change system that validates config diffs via policy simulation (dry-run), executes staged apply (canary -> ramp), continuously monitors cost/latency/quality signals, and performs automatic progressive rollbacks when guardrails are violated. This ticket covers design, an initial implementation in the runtime control plane, and an end-to-end test harness integrated with the console rollout UI and alerts.

Goals
- Prevent costly or latency-regressing config changes from impacting production at scale by catching them early with lightweight simulation and safe apply paths.
- Provide deterministic triggers and hysteresis so transient noise doesn't cause oscillation.
- Ensure state reconciliation when an automatic rollback or partial apply leaves config divergence between control plane and serving nodes.
- Surface batching/caching recommendations as part of policy checks so cost-saving proposals can be automatically tested in dry-run mode.

Non-goals
- This ticket does not implement global policy authoring UI; it consumes rules authored by PM/Policy team.
- Not covering RBAC/enterprise consent flows in depth; follow-up ticket will wire consent for private deployments.

Design overview
1) Pre-apply policy simulation (dry-run): when a config change is created (e.g., change batching.max_batch_size, kv_cache.ttl, q4_quantize=true), the control plane runs a simulated evaluation against recent traffic samples (last 30m/1h) to estimate token throughput, expected latency p50/p95, and cost delta. Simulation uses a lightweight model of the runtime: batching distribution, kv cache hit rate delta, and kernel selection impact.
2) Canary staged apply: if simulation passes soft thresholds, rollout applies to a small canary pool (1-3% of capacity) for a configurable window. During canary we collect actual metrics.
3) Guardrails & triggers: Automatic rollback triggers on deterministic conditions with hysteresis: 
   - latency_regression: p95 latency increase > 15% sustained for > 10m OR absolute increase > 150ms
   - cost_spike: per-token cost increase > 20% sustained for > 30m
   - error_rate: 5xx or model failure rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline
   - quality_regression: evaluation set perplexity or recall drop > configured threshold (only for models with eval harness)
   - safety_panic: manual 'panic' flag set by oncall or automated incident pipeline
4) Progressive rollback strategy: rollback proceeds in steps to avoid sudden capacity loss: revert canary first, then graded revert for ramped stages. Each step includes post-rollback verification window.
5) State reconciliation: after rollback, reconcile desired config (control plane) vs observed config on serving nodes. If divergence exists (partial apply), trigger a reconciliation worker that can: re-deploy the intended config, force a idempotent revert API call, or, if necessary, drain and rotate affected nodes. The reconciliation worker records audit events and retries with exponential backoff.

Key trade-offs considered
- Simulation fidelity vs cost: we limit simulation sample size to recent 30m and use a statistical model to reduce compute cost. This trades some accuracy for speed.
- Aggressive rollback thresholds vs false positives: we added hysteresis and minimum sample sizes to reduce oscillation.
- Progressive rollback complexity vs recovery speed: progressive rollback may slow recovery for large fleets but reduces risk of cold caches and throughput cliffs.

Acceptance criteria
- Dry-run simulation returns deterministic pass/fail and cost/latency delta estimates within +/-10% of canary observed values for 80% of experiments (measured on historical A/B datasets).
- Canary rollout obeys staged percentages and can be automatically rolled back by system-triggered guardrails without manual intervention.
- State reconciliation worker resolves 95% of partial apply divergences within 15 minutes without manual intervention; unresolved cases create an incident and attach a diagnostic bundle.
- Audit trail of config changes, simulation outputs, canary metrics, triggers, and rollback actions are visible in the Console and linked in the change history.

Implementation plan (milestones)
- Week 1: Design doc and policy rule schema (confluence). Create simulation harness to run on synthetic traffic and historical traces.
- Week 2: Implement pre-apply simulation runner and store outputs on change object; build Console UI hooks to display simulation results.
- Week 3: Implement canary staged apply in control plane + metrics collection hooks. Add guardrail evaluator service.
- Week 4: Implement progressive rollback actions and reconciliation worker; add audit logging.
- Week 5: E2E tests, canary on non-critical tenant, monitoring dashboards and alerts.
- Week 6: Documentation, runbook, and handoff to oncall.

Open decisions
- Threshold tuning: initial thresholds proposed above; need PM/RE team to review with historical cost/latency datasets.
- Simulations for quantized model changes: need input from runtime kernel team about cost multipliers for Q4/Q5 quantization.
- Reconciliation action escalation: when should we escalate to draining nodes vs repeating API calls?

Links and artifacts
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Config+Circuit+Breaker+Design
- PR for simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/2834
- Canary orchestration prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/142
- Grafana dashboard (canary metrics): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/Canary/Config-Canary
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/config-circuit-breaker

Rollout plan and monitoring
- Start with internal non-critical tenants (alpha) for 2 weeks with verbose logging.
- Promote to opt-in customers (beta) with a feature flag and provide explicit rollback override.
- After 6 weeks of stable alpha/beta runs, enable default for hosted API with conservative thresholds and long monitoring windows.

Risks and mitigations
- False positives causing unnecessary rollback: mitigate with hysteresis, minimum sample windows, and human override.
- Simulation mismatch for rare workloads: allow 'skip simulation' flag for experts and require manual review for high-impact customers.
- Reconciliation failures on VPC/private installs: add provider-specific apply/retry logic and work with infra team on safe restart procedures.
